### Blueprint sync issues

When the LaTeX blueprint is out of sync with Lean code, open an issue with
the `blueprint-sync` label. Describe which chapter, theorem, or definition
needs `\lean{}` / `\leanok` tags.

Automated drift detection: the [blueprint ↔ Lean sync check][ci-sync] runs
on every PR and fails when a `\leanok` tag sits on a Lean declaration whose
transitive axiom closure still depends on `sorryAx`. See
[`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`][ci-sync] for what it checks and how to run it
locally.

[ci-sync]: ci-blueprint-sync.md

### Stale-issue audits

Issues that cite specific `sorry` sites, file/line locations, or declaration
names drift out of date as `main` moves. Keep those citations precise rather
than replacing them with vague prose: update paths, line numbers, theorem labels,
and short source paraphrases when the source moves. Before starting a new
proof-closing round (or periodically as maintenance), run the audit script to
list open issues whose citations no longer resolve:

```bash
gh issue list --repo LionSR/MIPStarRE --state open --limit 500 \
  --json number,title,body,url,labels > /tmp/open-issues.json
python3 scripts/audit_stale_issues.py --issues /tmp/open-issues.json
```

The tool is report-only. Human review decides which flags warrant closing
the issue, updating its body, or dismissing as a false positive. A weekly
read-only GitHub Actions wrapper runs the same export-and-audit sequence and
uploads an artifact only when citations are flagged. See
[`docs/stale_issue_audit.md`](stale_issue_audit.md) for the full workflow.

---

## 3. Commit Messages

- Use **imperative mood** in the subject line ("Add", not "Added").
- Keep the subject under 72 characters.
- When squash-merging a PR, the commit message should match the PR title format.
- Reference issue numbers where applicable (`(#N)` suffix or `Addresses #N` in body).

---

## 4. Label Taxonomy

This section mirrors the labels that currently exist in the GitHub repository.
If this file and `gh label list` diverge, treat GitHub as the source of truth
and update this guide in the same PR. Most formalization issues combine
`formalization` + `2009.12982` with one or more chapter or theorem-family labels.
Documentation- or tooling-only issues usually skip the paper label. Do **not**
apply legacy labels such as `self-improvement`, `expansion-graph`,
`quantum-foundations`, or `automation`: those names are not part of the live
label set.

### Core work-type labels

| Label            | Description                                                |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `formalization`  | Lean formalization of a mathematical statement             |
| `documentation`  | Documentation-only work                                    |
| `infrastructure` | Foundational definitions, shared APIs, or supporting layers |
| `cleanup`        | Small cleanup, consistency, or style fix                   |
| `refactor`       | Structural change without intended behavior change         |
| `ci`             | CI/CD workflow or repository automation change             |

### Chapter / theorem-family labels

| Label               | Description                                                     |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ldt-basic`         | Early LDT definitions and low-degree-test scaffolding           |
| `preliminaries`     | Preliminaries chapter / section work                            |
| `commutativity`     | Commutativity chapters and related lemmas                       |
| `pasting`           | Pasting chapter and downstream chains                           |
| `main-induction`    | Main induction step                                             |
| `proof`             | Issue is primarily about proving an existing result             |
| `proof-infra`       | Intermediate lemmas or definitions that mainly support proofs   |
| `sorry-elimination` | Explicitly aimed at discharging remaining `sorry` sites         |
| `statement-fix`     | Paper-to-Lean statement correction / weakening / realignment    |
| `mismatch`          | Explicit paper-code mismatch audit or repair                    |
| `blueprint`         | Blueprint authoring or blueprint-expansion work                 |
| `blueprint-sync`    | Blueprint ↔ Lean synchronization issue                          |

### Paper labels

|--------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `2009.12982` | The main LDT paper tracked in this repository        |

| `blueprint-only` | Content exclusive to the blueprint (not in the original paper)   |

Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:

   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.

   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`

   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from

# MIPStarRE-local convention addenda

The canonical convention documents live in the `lean-conventions` skill of
[texra-ai/texra-lean-skills](https://github.com/texra-ai/texra-lean-skills)
(auto-installed for Claude Code sessions via `.claude/settings.json`; other
agents: clone the repository and symlink the skill directories, per its
README). This file holds only
MIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared
rules never move here.

## Style (MATHLIB_style)

### Linter warnings

Do not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add
broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide
blocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real
maintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.

Fix the warning at its source whenever possible:

- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;
- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass
  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;
- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;
- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than
  silencing `linter.flexible`.

If a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting
exception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably
`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.
Such exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as
the main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.

## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)

### Source-faithfulness checks

For this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean
statement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before
applying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions
`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed
source-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the
corresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.

Reject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,
repair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,
or arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as
positivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal
encodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when
mathematically load-bearing.

Reviewers should also inspect `\lean{}` and `\leanok` links.  A source-labelled
blueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction
theorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.
Auxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the
remark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.

## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)

### Companion document

> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues
> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the
> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still
> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,
> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default
> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
> Consult it alongside this file during review.

### Project paper-realignment protocol

The canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions
`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as
follows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in
`AGENTS.md`):

> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be
> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
> conditional helper
> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.

### Axiom policy

When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
the axiomatic base.

This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
faithful to the paper.

### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization

This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.

Signs to watch for:

- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
  incompatible universes)

When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
progress rather than enabling it.

### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift

A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
documented mathematical necessity.

The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.

Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.

Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.

Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
step of the source proof.

For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:

- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.

### Source-statement proof gaps

**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
      implementation-phase labels)?
- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
      source does not use them that way?
- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
      that order of preference?
- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
      construction they support?
- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.

Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
relevant audit before changing names or prose.

   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.

    13	# Section 5 — Locality-preserving projectivization repair
    14	
    15	This file proves the locality-preserving repair route for the late Section 5
    16	`Q/X/XHat/P` argument.
    17	
    18	## Scope
    19	
    20	The **spectral-truncation stage** (the first part of the proof of rounding
    21	to projectors) is already proved by
    22	`spectralTruncationStatement_of_sourceAlmostProjective` in
    23	`MakingMeasurementsProjective/SpectralTruncation/ProjectiveNonMeasurement.lean`,
    24	which is fully proved via
    25	`projectiveNonMeasurement_of_sourceAlmostProjective_full`. Proofs that
    26	require the spectral truncation statement should call that declaration directly.
    27	
    28	The main result recorded here:
    29	
    30	- **`leftLiftedProjectivizationRepair`** — paper origin
    31	  `references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex` lines 534–860 (rank
    32	  reduction and the `Q`/`√Q` completeness setup) and 862–1194 (the
    33	  `X`/`X̂`/`P` algebra producing the lifted projective sub-measurement,
    34	  including the final triangle-inequality assembly).  The formal proof below
    35	  follows that local `Q/X/XHat/P` route by passing to the left marginal state,
    36	  constructing the local projective family there, and transporting the final
    37	  estimate back to left lifts.
    38	
    39	The theorem proved here is the direct output of that route under a normalized
    40	bipartite state and the source almost-projective estimate for the left-lifted
    41	measurement. It is stated directly in terms of this estimate, rather than in
    42	terms of a separate repair-input assumption, and provides the unconditional
    43	repair step used by the orthonormalization theorem.
    44	-/

    54	/-- The diagonal block of a bipartite operator at a fixed right index. -/
    55	private def diagBlock {ιA ιB : Type*}
    56	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    57	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) (b : ιB) :
    58	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA :=
    59	  M.submatrix (fun i => (i, b)) (fun j => (j, b))

    61	/-- The normalized left marginal of a bipartite density, obtained by
    62	averaging its diagonal right blocks. -/
    63	private def leftMarginalDensity {ιA ιB : Type*}
    64	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
    65	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA :=
    66	  ((((Fintype.card ιB : Error) : Error)⁻¹ : Error) : ℂ) •
    67	    ∑ b : ιB, diagBlock ρ b

    69	/-- Positivity passes from a bipartite density to its left marginal. -/
    70	private lemma leftMarginalDensity_nonneg {ιA ιB : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
    72	    {ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) :
    73	    0 ≤ leftMarginalDensity ρ := by
    74	  have hρpsd : ρ.PosSemidef := Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hρ
    75	  have hsum : 0 ≤ ∑ b : ιB, diagBlock ρ b := by
    76	    refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => ?_
    77	    refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    78	    simpa [diagBlock] using hρpsd.submatrix (fun i => (i, b))
    79	  have hcoeff : 0 ≤ ((((Fintype.card ιB : Error) : Error)⁻¹ : Error) : ℂ) := by
    80	    positivity
    81	  simpa [leftMarginalDensity] using smul_nonneg hcoeff hsum

    93	/-- Left tensor placement is block diagonal with the same block at every

    95	private lemma leftTensor_eq_blockDiagonal_const {ιA ιB : Type*}
    96	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    97	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) :
    98	    leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) X = Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun _ : ιB => X) := by
    99	  ext x y
   100	  rcases x with ⟨i, b⟩
   101	  rcases y with ⟨j, c⟩
   102	  by_cases h : b = c
   103	  · subst c
   104	    simp [leftTensor, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
   105	  · simp [leftTensor, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply, h]

   107	/-- The trace against a constant block-diagonal operator is the sum of the
   108	traces of the diagonal blocks. -/
   109	private lemma trace_blockDiagonal_const_mul_eq_sum_trace_diagBlock
   110	    {ιA ιB : Type*}
   111	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   112	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA)
   113	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) :
   114	    Matrix.trace (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun _ : ιB => X) * M) =
   115	      ∑ b : ιB, Matrix.trace (X * diagBlock M b) := by
   116	  classical
   117	  let e : ((ιA × ιB) × ιA) ≃ (ιB × (ιA × ιA)) :=
   118	    { toFun := fun x => (x.1.2, (x.1.1, x.2))
   119	      invFun := fun x => ((x.2.1, x.1), x.2.2)
   120	      left_inv := fun ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩ => rfl
   121	      right_inv := fun ⟨_, ⟨_, _⟩⟩ => rfl }
   122	  simpa [diagBlock, Matrix.trace, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,
   123	    Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_sigma', e] using
   124	    (e.sum_comp (fun y : ιB × (ιA × ιA) =>
   125	      X y.2.1 y.2.2 * M (y.2.2, y.1) (y.2.1, y.1)))

   127	/-- Evaluating a local operator against the left marginal agrees with

   129	private lemma normalizedTrace_leftMarginalDensity_mul_eq
   130	    {ιA ιB : Type*}
   131	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
   132	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) :
   133	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (leftMarginalDensity ρ * X) =
   134	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ * leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) X) := by
   135	  have hcard : ((Fintype.card ιB : Error) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
   136	    exact_mod_cast Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   137	  unfold MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace leftMarginalDensity
   138	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum]
   139	  have hswap :
   140	      ∑ b : ιB, Matrix.trace (diagBlock ρ b * X) =
   141	        ∑ b : ιB, Matrix.trace (X * diagBlock ρ b) := by
   142	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   143	    intro b _
   144	    exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   145	  rw [hswap]
   146	  rw [Matrix.trace_mul_comm]
   147	  rw [leftTensor_eq_blockDiagonal_const]
   148	  rw [trace_blockDiagonal_const_mul_eq_sum_trace_diagBlock]
   149	  simp [Fintype.card_prod]

   282	**Faithful encoding:** This is an internal scalar estimate for the proved

   285	private lemma projectivizationRepair_small_error_bound {ζ : Error}
   286	    (hζ : 0 ≤ ζ) (hζ_small : ζ ≤ 1 / (4 : Error)) :
   287	    2 * (roundingToProjectiveError ζ + 30 * zetaQuarterRoot ζ) ≤
   288	      orthonormalizationMainLemmaError ζ := by
   289	  have htrunc : spectralTruncationError ζ ≤ zetaQuarterRoot ζ :=
   290	    spectralTruncationError_le_zetaQuarterRoot ζ hζ hζ_small
   291	  have hround : roundingToProjectiveError ζ ≤ 12 * zetaQuarterRoot ζ := by
   292	    dsimp [roundingToProjectiveError]
   293	    gcongr
   294	    simpa [spectralTruncationError, zetaQuarterRoot] using htrunc
   295	  calc
   296	    2 * (roundingToProjectiveError ζ + 30 * zetaQuarterRoot ζ)
   297	        ≤ 2 * (12 * zetaQuarterRoot ζ + 30 * zetaQuarterRoot ζ) := by
   298	            gcongr
   299	    _ = orthonormalizationMainLemmaError ζ := by
   300	          dsimp [orthonormalizationMainLemmaError, zetaQuarterRoot]
   301	          ring

   303	private lemma roundingToProjectiveError_le_orthonormalizationMainLemmaError {ζ : Error}
   304	    (hζ : 0 ≤ ζ) (hζ_small : ζ ≤ 1 / (4 : Error)) :
   305	    roundingToProjectiveError ζ ≤ orthonormalizationMainLemmaError ζ := by
   306	  have htrunc : spectralTruncationError ζ ≤ zetaQuarterRoot ζ :=

     7	/-!
     8	# Projective rounding for consistent POVMs
     9	
    10	This module proves the orthonormalization lemma `lem:ortho` with an explicit
    11	error constant: if a POVM `Q` on Alice's space and a POVM `R` on Bob's space are
    12	`δ`-consistent on a unit bipartite state `ψ`, then Alice has a projective
    13	measurement `P` on her original space with `P_a ⊗ 1` within `220 · δ^(1/4)` of
    14	`Q_a ⊗ 1` on `ψ`.
    15	
    16	The argument passes to Alice's reduced state and follows the construction of the
    17	LDT orthonormalization theorem. Rounding the almost-projective effects of `Q` and
    18	reducing their ranks gives a family of projectors `Q_a` whose ranges are almost
    19	orthogonal; assembling those ranges into one auxiliary space gives an operator
    20	`X`, whose positive-Gram polar factor `X̂` is a coisometry; and pulling the block
    21	projector of each outcome back along `X̂`, so that `P_a = X̂ᴴ T_a X̂`, gives a
    22	projective family close to `Q`. The family `P` lives on Alice's original space
    23	and is completed to a measurement at one fixed outcome once its missing state
    24	mass has been shown to be small.

95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}
   113	
   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

     2	\section{Making measurements projective}
     3	\label{sec:making-measurements-projective}
     4	
     5	A recurring theme in $\MIP^*$ research is that 
     6	projective measurements are significantly easier to manipulate
     7	than general POVM measurements.
     8	As just one example among many,
     9	when $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ are projective measurements,
    10	the ``$\approx_\delta$" and ``$\simeq_\delta$" distances are equivalent.
    11	In other words:
    12	\begin{equation*}
    13	A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a
    14	\qquad
    15	\iff
    16	\qquad
    17	A^x_a \ot I \approx_{2\delta} I \ot B^x_a.
    18	\end{equation*}
    19	This is Fact~$4.13$ from~\cite{NW19}.
    20	On the other hand when~$A$ and~$B$
    21	are not projective,
    22	one can find examples of measurements
    23	where $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$
    24	for $\delta \rightarrow 0$
    25	but one can show $A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\eps} I \ot B^x_a$
    26	only for $\eps \rightarrow 1$;
    27	this is Remark~$4.15$ from~\cite{NW19}.
    28	As a result, it is important to be able to convert
    29	POVM measurements to projective measurements
    30	whenever possible.
    31	
    32	In this section, we will survey two tools for doing so.
    33	The first of these is the textbook Naimark dilation theorem.
    34	In our setting, it states the following.
    35	
    36	\begin{theorem}[Naimark dilation]\label{thm:naimark}
    37	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
    38	Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}}$
    39	and $B=\{B^y_b\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
    40	Then there exists
    41	\begin{enumerate}
    42	\item Hilbert spaces $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$ and $\calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    43	\item a state $\ket{\mathsf{aux}} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    44	\item and two measurements  $\widehat{A} = \{\widehat{A}^x_a\}$ and $\widehat{B}=\{\widehat{B}^y_b\}$
    45	acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$
    46	and $\calH_{\mathrm{B}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    47	respectively,
    48	\end{enumerate}
    49	such that the following is true.
    50	If we write $\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}}$,
    51	then for all $x,y, a, b$,
    52	 \begin{equation*}
    53	 \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}
    54	 = \bra{\widehat{\psi}} \widehat{A}^x_a \ot \widehat{B}^y_b \ket{\widehat{\psi}}.
    55	 \end{equation*}
    56	 In addition, $\ket{\mathsf{aux}}$ is a \emph{product state},
    57	 meaning that we can write it as
    58	 \begin{equation*}
    59	 \ket{\mathsf{aux}}= \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}},
    60	 \end{equation*}
    61	for $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$
    62	and $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$.
    63	\end{theorem}
    64	The second of these is the ``orthogonalization lemma" from~\cite{KV11}.
    65	In the setting of symmetric strategies, it states the following.
    66	
    67	\begin{theorem}[Orthogonalization lemma]\label{thm:orthonormalization}
    68	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state,
    69	and let $A = \{A_a\}$ be a sub-measurement with strong self-consistency
    70	\begin{equation*}
    71	\sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes A_a \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\zeta.
    72	\end{equation*}
    73	Then there exists a projective sub-measurement $P = \{P_a\}$ such that
    74	\begin{equation*}
    75	A_a \otimes I \approx_{100 \zeta^{1/4}} P_a \otimes I.
    76	\end{equation*}
    77	\end{theorem}
    78	
    79	These two results serve largely the same purpose,
    80	and for our applications it will typically suffice to use either one.
    81	That said, there are tradeoffs when choosing to use one or the other.
    82	Naimark dilation is convenient because it can be applied to any family of sub-measurements
    83	and it preserves measurement outcome probabilities exactly.
    84	On the other hand, it requires swapping out the state $\ket{\psi}$ and measurements~$A$ and~$B$
    85	for $\ket{\widehat{\psi}}$ and $\widehat{A}$ and $\widehat{B}$, respectively,
    86	which can be notationally cumbersome.
    87	Most works opt to skip adding the hats,
    88	and instead say something to the effect of ``using Naimark, we can assume that~$A$ and~$B$ are projective."
    89	However, there is subtlety in doing so,
    90	which is that Naimark dilation does not necessarily preserve ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements;
    91	in other words, $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$
    92	does not necessarily imply $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$.
    93	(As an example, \Cref{ex:easy-but-long} below
    94	provides a case in which $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{0} I \ot B^x_a$,
    95	but $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$ only holds for $\delta \geq 1$.)
    96	This can lead to trouble if the same notation is used for~$A, B$ and $\widehat{A}, \widehat{B}$,
    97	as ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements derived before applying Naimark might not necessarily hold after applying Naimark.
    98	(That said, as pointed out at the end of Section~$4.4$ of~\cite{NW19},
    99	``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements are often derived as a consequence of ``$\simeq_{\delta}$" statements.
   100	And as Naimark preserves ``$\simeq_{\delta}$" statements,
   101	one could use them to simply rederive any ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements post-Naimark.)
   102	
   103	The downsides of using the orthogonalization lemma
   104	are that it can only be applied to measurements which are strongly self-consistent
   105	and it introduces additional error.
   106	As we will see below, its proof is significantly more complicated than Naimark dilation.
   107	On the plus side, it has none of the notational baggage that Naimark brings,
   108	and so it is more concrete to use.
   109	In addition, it can lead to stronger results,
   110	as it does not require introducing an auxiliary state $\ket{\mathsf{aux}}$.
   111	
   112	In this work, we will opt to use the orthogonalization lemma rather than Naimark dilation.
   113	However, we will include proofs of both for completeness.
   114	We will prove \Cref{thm:naimark} in \Cref{sec:naimark}
   115	and then \Cref{thm:orthonormalization} in \Cref{sec:orthogonalization}.
   116	
   117	\subsection{Naimark dilation}\label{sec:naimark}
   118	
   119	To prove \Cref{thm:naimark}, we will first need the following lemma.
   120	
   121	\begin{lemma}
   122	  \label{lem:naimark-helper}
   123	  Let $A = \{A_{a}\}$ be a sub-measurement with $k$ distinct outcomes $a \in \calA$, and let $\ket{\mathsf{aux}} \in \C^{k+1}$ be any state. Then there exists a projective sub-measurement $\widehat{A} = \{\widehat{A}_{a}\}$ such that
   124	  for each outcome~$a$,
   125	  \[ (I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot \widehat{A}_{a} \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}}) =
   126	    A_{a}. \]
   127	\end{lemma}
   128	\begin{proof}
   129	We will consider an orthonormal basis for $\C^{k+1}$
   130	consisting of a vector $\ket{a}$ for each $a \in \calA$ and the vector $\ket{\bot}$.
   131	Let~$U$ be any unitary such that for each vector $\ket{\psi} \in \C^d$,
   132	\begin{align*}
   133	U \cdot (\ket{\psi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   134	&= \sum_{a \in \calA} ((A_{a})^{1/2} \ket{\psi}) \ot \ket{a} + ((1 - A)^{1/2}\ket{\psi}) \ot \ket{\bot}\\
   135	&= \Big(\sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}\Big)
   136			\cdot \ket{\psi}.
   137	\end{align*}
   138	This implies that
   139	\begin{equation*}
   140	U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   141	= \sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}.
   142	\end{equation*}
   143	Hence, for any $a \in \calA$,
   144	\begin{equation*}
   145	(I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   146	= (I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot \Big(\sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}\Big)
   147	= (A_a)^{1/2}.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	  Then the desired projective sub-measurement is
   150	  \[ \widehat{A}_a = U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a} \bra{a}) \cdot U. \]
   151	  This is because
   152	\begin{align*}
   153	 (I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot \widehat{A}_{a} \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   154	&=(I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot (U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a} \bra{a}) \cdot U) \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})\\
   155	&=(I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a}) \cdot (I\ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})\\
   156	&= (A_a)^{1/2} \cdot (A_a)^{1/2} = A_a.
   157	\end{align*}
   158	This completes the proof.
   159	\end{proof}
   160	
   161	Now we prove \Cref{thm:naimark}.
   162	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:naimark}]
   163	For each $x$, let $k$ be the number of outcomes in $A^x$,
   164	and let $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}}$ be a state of dimensionality $k+1$.
   165	Let $\widetilde{A}^x$ be the sub-measurement guaranteed by \Cref{lem:naimark-helper}.
   166	Define $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},x}}$ and $\widetilde{B}^x$ similarly.
   167	We define
   168	\begin{equation*}
   169	\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi} \ot \big(\ot_{x} \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}}\big)
   170						\ot \big(\ot_{x} \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},x}}\big)
   171	\end{equation*}
   172	and
   173	\begin{align*}
   174	\widehat{A}^x_a
   175	&= \widetilde{A}^x_a \ot \big(\ot_{z \neq x} I_{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},z}}\big)\\
   176	\widehat{B}^y_b
   177	&= \widetilde{B}^y_b \ot \big(\ot_{z\neq y} I_{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},z}}\big).
   178	\end{align*}
   179	Then for all $x,y,z,b$,
   180	\begin{align*}
   181	\bra{\widehat{\psi}} \widehat{A}^x_a \ot \widehat{B}^y_b \ket{\widehat{\psi}}
   182	& = \bra{\psi} \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}} \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},y}}
   183		\cdot \widetilde{A}^x_a \ot \widetilde{B}^y_b \cdot \ket{\psi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},y}}\\
   184	&= 	\bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}.
   185	\end{align*}
   186	This completes the proof.
   187	\end{proof}
   188	
   189	\begin{example}[Naimark does not preserve ``$\approx_{\delta}$'']\label{ex:easy-but-long}
   190	We now carry out a simple example
   191	in which Naimark preserves ``$\simeq_\delta$'' statements without preserving ``$\approx_\delta$'' statements.
   192	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be an arbitrary state in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$,
   193	where $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} = \calH_{\mathrm{B}} = \C^d$.
   194	In addition, let $A = \{A_0, A_1\}$ and $B = \{B_0, B_1\}$ be the two-outcome measurements
   195	in which $A_0 = A_1 = B_0 = B_1 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot I_{d \times d}$.
   196	Then
   197	\begin{align*}
   198	\sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A_a \ot B_b\ket{\psi}
   199	&= \bra{\psi} A_0 \ot B_1\ket{\psi} + \bra{\psi} A_1 \ot B_0\ket{\psi}\\
   200	&= \frac{1}{4} \cdot \bra{\psi} I \ot I \ket{\psi} + \frac{1}{4} \cdot \bra{\psi} I \ot I \ket{\psi}
   201	= \frac{1}{2},
   202	\end{align*}
   203	and so $A_a \ot I \simeq_{1/2} I \ot A_a$.
   204	In addition,
   205	\begin{equation*}
   206	\sum_a \Vert (A_a \ot I - I \ot B_a) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2
   207	= \sum_a \Big\Vert \Big(\frac{1}{2} \cdot I \ot I - \frac{1}{2} \cdot I \ot I\Big) \ket{\psi}\Big\Vert^2
   208	= 0,
   209	\end{equation*}
   210	and so $A_a \ot I \approx_0 I \ot B_a$.
   211	
   212	Now we carry out the steps of Naimark dilation.
   213	Because~$A$ and~$B$ are two-outcome,
   214	we will set $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}} = \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}} = \C^2$,
   215	spanned by the basis vectors $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{1}$.
   216	(\Cref{lem:naimark-helper} actually asks that the auxiliary space have dimension $2+1 = 3$,
   217	where the third dimension is spanned by the basis vector $\ket{\bot}$.
   218	However, this is unnecessary for this example because~$A$ and~$B$
   219	are measurements rather than sub-measurements.)
   220	We will choose our two local auxiliary states
   221	to be
   222	\begin{equation*}
   223	\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} = \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}}
   224		= \ket{+} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ket{0} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ket{1}.
   225	\end{equation*}
   226	We first construct $\widehat{A}$ by following the proof of \Cref{lem:naimark-helper}.
   227	To begin, it asks for~$U$ to be a unitary such that for any $\ket{\phi}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}}$,
   228	\begin{align*}
   229	U \cdot (\ket{\phi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}})
   230	&=U \cdot (\ket{\phi} \ot \ket{+})\\
   231	&=  ((A_{0})^{1/2} \ket{\phi}) \ot \ket{0} + ((A_{1})^{1/2} \ket{\phi}) \ot \ket{1}\\
   232	&= \Big(\Big(\frac{1}{2}\cdot I\Big)^{1/2} \ket{\phi}\Big) \ot \ket{0}
   233		+ \Big(\Big(\frac{1}{2}\cdot I\Big)^{1/2} \ket{\phi}\Big) \ot \ket{1}\\
   234	&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \ket{\phi} \ot \ket{0} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \ket{\phi} \ot \ket{1}\\

   494	/-- A consistent pair of POVMs admits an Alice-side projective rounding with
   495	the explicit dimension-independent error `220 * δ^(1/4)`. -/
   496	theorem projective_rounding_with_explicit_constant {ιA ιB α : Type*}
   497	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   498	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   499	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
   500	    (Q : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA)
   501	    (R : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB) (δ : Error) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
   502	    (hcons : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   503	      (fun _ a => heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1)
   504	      (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (R.effect a)) ψ ≤ δ) :
   505	    ∃ Pm : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA,
   506	      MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective Pm ∧
   507	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   508	        (fun _ a => heteroKron (Pm.effect a) 1)
   509	        (fun _ a => heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1) ψ ≤
   510	          220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : Error) := by
   511	  have hι : Nonempty (ιA × ιB) := by
   512	    by_contra hempty
   513	    letI : IsEmpty (ιA × ιB) := not_nonempty_iff.mp hempty
   514	    have hzero : ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   515	    rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hψ
   516	    norm_num at hψ
   517	  haveI : Nonempty ιA := ⟨(Classical.choice hι).1⟩
   518	  haveI : Nonempty ιB := ⟨(Classical.choice hι).2⟩
   519	  have hα : Nonempty α := round_measurement_outcome_nonempty Q
   520	  letI : Nonempty α := hα
   521	  let a₀ : α := Classical.choice hα
   522	  let Ψ : PureState (ιA × ιB) := roundPureState ψ hψ
   523	  let HA : FiniteHilbertSpace := roundFiniteHilbertSpace ιA
   524	  let HB : FiniteHilbertSpace := roundFiniteHilbertSpace ιB
   525	  let A : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement α ιA :=
   526	    MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement (H := HA) Q
   527	  let B : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement α ιB :=
   528	    MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement (H := HB) R
   529	  have hCons : ConsRel (Ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) (uniformDistribution Unit)
   530	      (constSubMeasFamily A.toSubMeas) (constSubMeasFamily B.toSubMeas) δ := by
   531	    simpa [Ψ, HA, HB, A, B] using
   532	      round_consRel_of_consistencyDefect ψ hψ Q R δ hcons
   533	  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := round_projective_ldt (Ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
   534	    Ψ.toQuantumState_isNormalized A B a₀ δ hδ hCons
   535	  let Pm : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA :=
   536	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne C.outcome C.outcome_pos <| by
   537	      rw [C.sum_eq_total, C.total_eq_one]
   538	  have hPm_projective : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective Pm := by
   539	    intro a
   540	    change IsProj (C.outcome a)
   541	    exact
   542	      { isIdempotentElem := C.proj a
   543	        isSelfAdjoint :=
   544	          (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (C.outcome_pos a)).isHermitian.eq }
   545	  refine ⟨Pm, hPm_projective, ?_⟩
   546	  have hdist :
   547	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   548	          (fun _ a => heteroKron (Pm.effect a) 1)
   549	          (fun _ a => heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1) ψ =
   550	        qSDD (Ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
   551	          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) C.toSubMeas)
   552	          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) A.toSubMeas) := by
   553	    unfold opFamilyDistSq
   554	    rw [show avgOver (uniformDistribution Unit)
   555	        (fun _ => ∑ a : α,
   556	          ‖applyOperatorToState
   557	            (heteroKron (Pm.effect a) 1 - heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1) ψ‖ ^ 2) =
   558	        ∑ a : α,
   559	          ‖applyOperatorToState
   560	            (heteroKron (Pm.effect a) 1 - heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1) ψ‖ ^ 2 by
   561	      simp [avgOver, uniformDistribution]]
   562	    unfold qSDD qSDDCore
   563	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   564	    intro a _
   565	    rw [round_ev_adjoint_mul_self_eq_norm_sq ψ hψ]
   566	    simp only [Pm, A, HA, leftPlacedSubMeas, mkLeftPlacedSubMeas_outcome,
   567	      MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement_outcome,
   568	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne]
   569	    rfl
   570	  rw [hdist]

     7	/-!
     8	# Projective rounding for consistent POVMs
     9	
    10	This module proves the orthonormalization lemma `lem:ortho` with an explicit
    11	error constant: if a POVM `Q` on Alice's space and a POVM `R` on Bob's space are
    12	`δ`-consistent on a unit bipartite state `ψ`, then Alice has a projective
    13	measurement `P` on her original space with `P_a ⊗ 1` within `220 · δ^(1/4)` of
    14	`Q_a ⊗ 1` on `ψ`.
    15	
    16	The argument passes to Alice's reduced state and follows the construction of the
    17	LDT orthonormalization theorem. Rounding the almost-projective effects of `Q` and
    18	reducing their ranks gives a family of projectors `Q_a` whose ranges are almost
    19	orthogonal; assembling those ranges into one auxiliary space gives an operator
    20	`X`, whose positive-Gram polar factor `X̂` is a coisometry; and pulling the block
    21	projector of each outcome back along `X̂`, so that `P_a = X̂ᴴ T_a X̂`, gives a
    22	projective family close to `Q`. The family `P` lives on Alice's original space
    23	and is completed to a measurement at one fixed outcome once its missing state
    24	mass has been shown to be small.
    25	
    26	## References
    27	
    28	- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:131-153`
    29	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:390-423` (`lem:ortho`)
    30	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:425-470`
    31	  (`lem:ortho-explicit-constant`, the statement proved in this module)
    32	- `references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex`
    33	-/

    45	/-- The normalized pure state whose vector is the given unit Euclidean vector. -/
    46	private noncomputable def roundPureState {ι : Type*}
    47	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    48	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) : PureState ι where
    49	  vector := ψ.ofLp
    50	  unit := by
    51	    calc
    52	      star ψ.ofLp ⬝ᵥ ψ.ofLp = ψ.ofLp ⬝ᵥ star ψ.ofLp := dotProduct_comm _ _
    53	      _ = inner ℂ ψ ψ := (EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct ψ ψ).symm
    54	      _ = (‖ψ‖ ^ 2 : ℂ) := inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K ψ
    55	      _ = 1 := by rw [hψ]; norm_num

    57	/-- The QPBT vector quadratic form equals evaluation in `roundPureState`. -/
    58	private theorem round_stateQForm_eq_ev {ι : Type*}
    59	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    60	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (T : Op ι) :
    61	    stateQForm ψ T = ev (roundPureState ψ hψ : QuantumState ι) T := by
    62	  rw [PureState.ev_eq_re_inner]
    63	  simp only [roundPureState]
    64	  change (inner ℂ ψ (WithLp.toLp 2 (T *ᵥ ψ.ofLp))).re =
    65	    (star ψ.ofLp ⬝ᵥ T *ᵥ ψ.ofLp).re
    66	  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, dotProduct_comm]

    71	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (T : Op ι) :

    79	  change (inner ℂ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin T ψ) (Matrix.toEuclideanLin T ψ)).re =

  1454			Q_a \ot I \approx_{30\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \ot I.

   388	The following lemma shows that POVMs that are approximately projective, in
   389	the sense of being self-consistent, are close to exact projective
   390	measurements.
   391	
   392	\begin{lemma}[Orthonormalization lemma]
   393		\label{lem:ortho}
   394		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_projective_close_of_consistent}
   395		\leanok
   396		\uses{def:consistency, def:povm-distance}
   397		Let $0 \leq \delta \leq 1$. There exists a function
   398		$\eta_{\mathrm{ortho}}(\delta) = O\big(\delta^{1/4}\big)$ such that the
   399		following holds. Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state on
   400		$\hilb_{\mathsf{A}} \ot \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}$ where $\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$
   401		and $\hilb_{\mathsf{B}}$ are finite dimensional, and let $\{Q_a\}$ and
   402		$\{R_a\}$ be POVMs on $\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$ and $\hilb_{\mathsf{B}}$
   403		respectively such that
   404		\begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-cond}
   405			Q_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \,\simeq_\delta\, \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot R_a\,.
   406		\end{equation}
   407		Then there exists a projective measurement $\{P_a\}$ on
   408		$\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$ such that, with respect to $\ket{\psi}$,
   409		\begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-ccl}
   410			P_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \,\approx_{\eta_{\mathrm{ortho}}(\delta)}\, Q_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}}\,.
   411		\end{equation}
   412	\end{lemma}
   413	\begin{proof}
   414		\leanok
   415		\uses{lem:ortho-explicit-constant}
   416		The source imports this lemma: it first appears in~\cite{KV11}, and a
   417		self-contained proof is given in the reference [ML20] cited
   418		in~\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. Here it is obtained from
   419		Lemma~\ref{lem:ortho-explicit-constant}, which exhibits
   420		$\eta_{\mathrm{ortho}}(\delta) = 220\,\delta^{1/4}$: passing to Alice's
   421		reduced state, the rank-reduction and orthonormalization construction of
   422		Chapter~\ref{chap:projective} produces a projective family on
   423		$\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$ close to $\{Q_a\}$, and completing that family at one
   424		fixed outcome yields the projective measurement $\{P_a\}$.
   425	\end{proof}
   426	
   427	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for Lemma~\ref{lem:ortho}]
   428		\label{lem:ortho-explicit-constant}
   429		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.projective_rounding_with_explicit_constant}
   430		\leanok
   431		\uses{def:consistency, def:povm-distance}
   432		This formalization-only auxiliary is not a named statement of the paper; it is
   433		the explicit-constant form of Lemma~\ref{lem:ortho} from which that lemma is
   434		obtained. Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a unit vector on
   435		$\hilb_{\mathsf{A}} \ot \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}$ with $\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$ and
   436		$\hilb_{\mathsf{B}}$ finite dimensional, let $\{Q_a\}$ and $\{R_a\}$ be POVMs
   437		on $\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$ and $\hilb_{\mathsf{B}}$ respectively, and let
   438		$\delta \geq 0$ satisfy the exact consistency-defect bound
   439		\[
   440		\operatorname{consistencyDefect}\!\left(
   441			\operatorname{uniformDistribution}(\mathrm{Unit}),
   442			(u,a) \mapsto Q_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}},
   443			(u,a) \mapsto \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot R_a,
   444			\ket{\psi}\right) \leq \delta\,.
   445		\]
   446		Then there is a projective measurement $\{P_a\}$ on $\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$ with
   447		\[
   448			\sum_{a}
   449			\left\|\left((P_a-Q_a) \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}}\right)\ket{\psi}\right\|^2
   450			\leq 220\,\delta^{1/4}\,.
   451		\]
   452	\end{lemma}
   453	\begin{proof}
   454		\leanok
   455		\uses{lem:projective-low-rank-sum, lem:Q-completeness, lem:P-Q-approx,
   456			def:projective-P}
   457		Work with Alice's reduced state $\rho_A$, for which the consistency
   458		hypothesis gives
   459		$\sum_a \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\rho_A(Q_a-Q_a^2)\right) \leq 2\delta$.
   460		When $\delta^{1/4} \leq 1/24$, rank reduction
   461		(Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}) replaces $\{Q_a\}$ by a family of
   462		projectors, Lemma~\ref{lem:Q-completeness} shows that this family is almost
   463		complete on $\rho_A$, and the operator $P$ of
   464		Definition~\ref{def:projective-P} is projective and close to it by
   465		Lemma~\ref{lem:P-Q-approx}. Completing $P$ at one fixed outcome and summing the
   466		two estimates gives the bound $220\,\delta^{1/4}$, the completion contributing
   467		the residual mass controlled by Lemma~\ref{lem:Q-completeness}. When
   468		$\delta^{1/4} > 1/24$, the bound $220\,\delta^{1/4} > 9$ exceeds the universal
   469		bound $4$ on the distance between any two sub-measurements on a normalized
   470		state, so the completion of the zero sub-measurement already satisfies the
   471		conclusion.
   472	\end{proof}

    54	/-- The diagonal block of a bipartite operator at a fixed right index. -/
    55	def diagBlock {ιA ιB : Type*}
    56	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    57	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) (b : ιB) :

    59	  M.submatrix (fun i => (i, b)) (fun j => (j, b))

    61	/-- The normalized left marginal of a bipartite density, obtained by
    62	averaging its diagonal right blocks. -/
    63	def leftMarginalDensity {ιA ιB : Type*}
    64	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
    65	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA :=
    66	  ((((Fintype.card ιB : Error) : Error)⁻¹ : Error) : ℂ) •
    67	    ∑ b : ιB, diagBlock ρ b

    69	/-- Positivity passes from a bipartite density to its left marginal. -/
    70	lemma leftMarginalDensity_nonneg {ιA ιB : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
    72	    {ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) :
    73	    0 ≤ leftMarginalDensity ρ := by
    74	  have hρpsd : ρ.PosSemidef := Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hρ
    75	  have hsum : 0 ≤ ∑ b : ιB, diagBlock ρ b := by
    76	    refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => ?_
    77	    refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    78	    simpa [diagBlock] using hρpsd.submatrix (fun i => (i, b))
    79	  have hcoeff : 0 ≤ ((((Fintype.card ιB : Error) : Error)⁻¹ : Error) : ℂ) := by
    80	    positivity
    81	  simpa [leftMarginalDensity] using smul_nonneg hcoeff hsum

    93	lemma leftTensor_eq_blockDiagonal_const {ιA ιB : Type*}
    94	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    95	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) :
    96	    leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) X = Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun _ : ιB => X) := by
    97	  ext x y
    98	  rcases x with ⟨i, b⟩
    99	  rcases y with ⟨j, c⟩
   100	  by_cases h : b = c
   101	  · subst c
   102	    simp [leftTensor, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
   103	  · simp [leftTensor, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply, h]

   105	/-- The trace against a constant block-diagonal operator is the sum of the
   106	traces of the diagonal blocks. -/
   107	lemma trace_blockDiagonal_const_mul_eq_sum_trace_diagBlock
   108	    {ιA ιB : Type*}
   109	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   110	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA)
   111	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) :
   112	    Matrix.trace (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun _ : ιB => X) * M) =
   113	      ∑ b : ιB, Matrix.trace (X * diagBlock M b) := by
   114	  classical
   115	  let e : ((ιA × ιB) × ιA) ≃ (ιB × (ιA × ιA)) :=
   116	    { toFun := fun x => (x.1.2, (x.1.1, x.2))
   117	      invFun := fun x => ((x.2.1, x.1), x.2.2)
   118	      left_inv := fun ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩ => rfl
   119	      right_inv := fun ⟨_, ⟨_, _⟩⟩ => rfl }
   120	  simpa [diagBlock, Matrix.trace, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,
   121	    Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_sigma', e] using
   122	    (e.sum_comp (fun y : ιB × (ιA × ιA) =>
   123	      X y.2.1 y.2.2 * M (y.2.2, y.1) (y.2.1, y.1)))

   125	/-- Evaluating a local operator against the left marginal agrees with
   126	evaluating its left tensor placement against the bipartite density. -/
   127	lemma normalizedTrace_leftMarginalDensity_mul_eq
   128	    {ιA ιB : Type*}
   129	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Nonempty ιB]
   130	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) :
   131	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (leftMarginalDensity ρ * X) =
   132	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ * leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) X) := by
   133	  have hcard : ((Fintype.card ιB : Error) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
   134	    exact_mod_cast Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   135	  unfold MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace leftMarginalDensity
   136	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum]
   137	  have hswap :
   138	      ∑ b : ιB, Matrix.trace (diagBlock ρ b * X) =
   139	        ∑ b : ιB, Matrix.trace (X * diagBlock ρ b) := by
   140	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   141	    intro b _
   142	    exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   143	  rw [hswap]
   144	  rw [Matrix.trace_mul_comm]
   145	  rw [leftTensor_eq_blockDiagonal_const]
   146	  rw [trace_blockDiagonal_const_mul_eq_sum_trace_diagBlock]
   147	  simp [Fintype.card_prod]
   148	  ring

   254	### Stale-issue audits
   255	
   256	Issues that cite specific `sorry` sites, file/line locations, or declaration
   257	names drift out of date as `main` moves. Keep those citations precise rather
   258	than replacing them with vague prose: update paths, line numbers, theorem labels,
   259	and short source paraphrases when the source moves. Before starting a new
   260	proof-closing round (or periodically as maintenance), run the audit script to
   261	list open issues whose citations no longer resolve:
   262	
   263	```bash
   264	gh issue list --repo LionSR/MIPStarRE --state open --limit 500 \
   265	  --json number,title,body,url,labels > /tmp/open-issues.json
   266	python3 scripts/audit_stale_issues.py --issues /tmp/open-issues.json
   267	```
   268	
   269	The tool is report-only. Human review decides which flags warrant closing
   270	the issue, updating its body, or dismissing as a false positive. A weekly
   271	read-only GitHub Actions wrapper runs the same export-and-audit sequence and
   272	uploads an artifact only when citations are flagged. See
   273	[`docs/stale_issue_audit.md`](stale_issue_audit.md) for the full workflow.

   377	   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag
   378	   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical
   379	   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,

   460	For semantic objects such as measurements, submeasurements, distributions,
   461	averaged operators, and packaged theorem outputs, reviewers should additionally

   463	
   464	1. **Impossible states check** -- Does the structure exclude states that are
   465	   impossible under the paper definition?
   466	2. **Derived-field check** -- If a field is mathematically derived
   467	   (e.g. `total = ∑ a, outcome a`), is it either derived on demand or stored
   468	   together with an equality proof (e.g. `sum_eq_total`)?

   470	   boundedness/normalization, completeness where applicable) encoded directly
   471	   in the structure or constructor, rather than deferred to downstream lemmas?

   473	   PR provable/stated against the scaffold without adding ad hoc assumptions?
